name: আপৎসহায়েশ্বরর মন্দির, তেনকুরঙ্গাড়ুতুরৈ
deity: আপৎসহায়েশ্বরর রূপে শিব, দেবী পবলক্কোড়ি অম্মৈ-র সঙ্গে
period: তেবারম যুগ (৭ম শতাব্দীতে গীত); পরবর্তী চোল কাঠামোগত মন্দির
summary: তেনকুরঙ্গাড়ুতুরৈ, কাবেরীর দক্ষিণ তীরে আড়ুতুরৈতে, শিবকে আপৎসহায়েশ্বরর রূপে — 'বিপদে সহায়' — দেবী পবলক্কোড়ি অম্মৈর সঙ্গে সম্মান করে। সম্বন্দর ও অপ্পর কর্তৃক গীত একটি পাডল পেট্র স্থলম্, এর উঁচু পাঁচ-স্তরের পশ্চিম গোপুরম কুম্বকোণমের কাছে বদ্বীপ অঞ্চলের উপর উঠে দাঁড়ায়।

sections.history: Thenkurangaduthurai, at Aduthurai in Thanjavur district, is a Paadal Petra Sthalam on the southern bank of the Kaveri, hymned in the Tevaram by Sambandar and Appar. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later; its western gopuram, the tallest, rises in five tiers to about 72 feet.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Apathsahayeswarar in the sanctum, with the goddess Pavalakkodi Ammai (Prabhavalli) in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The five-tiered western tower, about 72 feet, is the temple's landmark over the Aduthurai country.
sections.legends: The lord is worshipped as Apathsahayeswarar, 'the help in adversity,' the one who comes to the aid of those in distress; the goddess is Pavalakkodi Ammai, 'the coral creeper.' As with the delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana survives in local tradition and the Tevaram verses of Sambandar and Appar.
sections.festivals: The temple observes the Aippasi Annabishekam (October–November) as its most prominent festival, besides Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship.
sections.experience: At Thenkurangaduthurai the pilgrim comes to the help in adversity. Before Apathsahayeswarar and Pavalakkodi Ammai, beneath the tall western tower by the Kaveri's bank, the visitor finds the unhurried grace of a Tevaram temple of the Aduthurai delta.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Thenkurangaduthurai is at Aduthurai, in Thanjavur district, near the Kumbakonam–Mayiladuthurai road. Aduthurai and Kumbakonam are the nearest towns and rail heads, with buses and taxis to the temple.
